question.leadin: This ruler's most famous victory came at the Battle of Hattin.
question.text: Name this Kurdish ruler who founded the Ayyubid dynasty. He reconquered Jerusalem for the Islamic world in 1187.
question.answerHtml: Saladin [or Ṣalāḥ ad-Dīn, or Selahedîn, or Yusuf ibn Ayyub ibn Shadi]
question.clue: This man's namesake "tithe" was collected in England and France after he captured the city Baldwin was King of, and he famously offered Guy de Lusignan ice water after capturing him near an extinct volcano at the Battle of Hattin.

swap.leadin: Popular protest slogans during this time period often started with "Ash-shab yurid," meaning "the people want."
swap.text: Name this series of political movements in North Africa and the Middle East that began in December 2010.
swap.clue: One government destroyed the Pearl Roundabout, a gathering place for protests during this period.

question.leadin: Name the following Middle Eastern countries.
question.text: This country's city of Madaba is known for its Byzantine map depicting the Holy Land. The city of Aqaba is also in this "Hashemite Kingdom."
question.clue: Avi Shlaim famously alleged that this country's ruler colluded with David Ben-Gurion in 1948 to allow Israel to seize land, but in 1988 this country renounced its claims to the land it had occupied in 1948, and in 1994 it recognized Israel.

swap.text: This computer worm attacked Iran's Natanz uranium enrichment facilities and was the first discovered malware to subvert industrial systems.
swap.clue: This computer virus, likely sponsored by the United States and Israel, targeted Iran's nuclear program. This virus placed a rootkit on programmable logical controllers, ultimately destroying one-fifth of Iran's nuclear centrifuges.

question.leadin: Name these places where archaeological discoveries were announced in 2022.
question.text: An ivory comb bearing an ancient Canaanite (KAY-nuh-nyte) engraving was unearthed at Tel Lachish (TEL lah-KEESH) in this country. The mountaintop fortress of Masada (muh-SAH-dah) is also in this country.
question.clue: Along with Lehi , another paramilitary group carried out the Deir Yassin massacre in this modern-day country, although the Haganah criticized them for violating this country's "purity of arms" policy.

swap.text: This conflict during Ben-Gurion's tenure began when Israeli ships were blocked from the Straits of Tiran. Canadian Prime Minister Lester Pearson resolved this conflict in favor of Gamal Abdel Nasser.
swap.clue: Robert Menzies failed to end this event peacefully, leading to the bombing of troops under Abdel Hakim Amer in this event's Operation Musketeer.

question.leadin: This man was found with a gold-plated Browning Hi-Power pistol, referencing his son's Khamis Brigade, at the time of his capture.
question.text: Name this leader from Sirte, who came to power by overthrowing his country's King Idris. In 2003, this leader accepted responsibility for the Lockerbie bombing.
question.clue: This man was overthrown by the National Transitional Council after the Battle of Sirte ].

swap.text: This Turkish tribe migrated from Persia and their leader Togrul captured Baghdad from the Abbasid caliphate, expanding into Afghanistan and Central Asia before falling apart and being divided by invading Mongols in Anatolia in the mid 1300s. They won the battle of Manzikert.
swap.clue: This group captured the Aklat Fort, and thus Romanus IV, during their greatest military victory.

question.leadin: This group established the consecutive Bahri and Burji dynasties, which began after Aybak established a sultanate shortly before his murder by Shajar al-Durr.
question.text: Identify this military group that overthrew Turanshah and ended the Ayyubid dynasty after resisting Louis IX's crusade at the Battle of Fariskur.
question.answerHtml: Mamluks [or Mamelukes; despite the claims of Wikipedia, do not accept “Marmaduke,” who is a fictional dog and not a Muslim soldier]
question.clue: Barquq("bar-kuk")overthrew the last Kipchak ruler of these people and began their Circassian-dominated Burji ("bur-JEE") dynasty.

swap.leadin: These people founded the Sultanate of Rum over what had been Byzantine Anatolia.
swap.text: Name this Turkish dynasty which branched off from the Oghuz Turks. It was a major power in the Near and Middle East from its 11th-century victory at Manzikert into the early 14th century.
swap.clue: One offshoot of this dynastic group was the Sultanate of Rum.

question.text: Ahmad Sanjar, a later Seljuk Turk ruler, fought campaigns against these Ismaili Muslims whose name now describes their common action of covertly killing rulers they didn't like.

swap.leadin: His followers called themselves "al-Muwahhidun," which translates roughly as "Unitarians," and he is the author of the Kitab al-tawhid.
swap.text: Identify this man who first took a stand against innovation in his religion in 1736.
swap.clue: In his hometown of Uyaynah, he gained the favor of a ruler named Uthman, whom he directed to begin a campaign of iconoclasm, destroying the domes on the gravesites of Muhammad's companion.

question.text: The Banu Musa brothers worked alongside this scholar, who translated the Roman cartography treatise Geography into Arabic. Another treatise by this scholar introduced Indian numerals to the Arabic world.

swap.leadin: Among the events that occurred during his rule were a 1997 massacre at Deir el-Bahri, as well as engaging in a New Valley canal project in the same year.
swap.text: Name this ruler who helped mediate the 1993 agreement between Israel and the PLO and reaffirmed the Camp David Accords after the assassination of his predecessor.
swap.clue: This man served as vice president under Anwar Sadat, and it has been suggested that he played a part in Sadat's assassination.

question.text: Harun also destroyed the power of this family after one of its members impregnated his sister Abassa. This family patronized scholars such as Geber and was influential during the early years of the caliphate.
question.clue: The most upwardly mobile Persians belonged to this family, who had originally been Buddhist administrators in the Balkh region. The use of this family's name to describe an imaginary feast may relate from an anti-Persian attack on their false hospitality.

swap.text: This Egyptian educational institution was made into a public university in 1961. It has long been a prominent center of religious scholarship alongside a mosque of the same name.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Homs-based warfare in the latter 13th century.
question.text: The frst two Battles of Homs in 1260 and 1281 CE pitted the Ilkhanate against forces of this slave dynasty led by the Sul-tans Qalawun and Baybars, who won a big victory for them at Ayn Jalut.

swap.leadin: This man provided refuge for the German diplomat Fritz Grobba, and was persuaded by his adviser Harry St. John Philby to award concessions to American companies.
swap.text: Name this man who conquered Najd and the Hejaz, and defeated the Ikhwan, before consolidating his holdings and founding a kingdom in 1932.
swap.answerHtml: Ibn Saud [or Abdulaziz ibn Abdul Rahman ibn Faisal ibn Turki ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Saud; or Abdulaziz]
swap.clue: This man lost some foreign backing after the Battle of Jarrab, where his advisor William Shakespear was killed by the rival Rashid family.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a crusade, FTPE.
question.text: In this crusade, the forces of Leopold VI of Austria and Andrew II of Hungary met that of John of Brienne in Jerusalem and began a successful campaign in Egypt. A continued push towards Cairo failed, and they were crushed at the Battle of al-Mansura.
question.clue: Pope Honorius II oversaw the end of this campaign against the Ayyubids that was called in 1213.

swap.leadin: This man consolidated military forces in his country by leading a surprise attack on the Tigers Militia in the Safra Massacre.
swap.text: Name this leader of a non-Spanish Phalange Party who, with the help of US Ambassador Philip Habib, gained American support after becoming president in 1982.
swap.clue: This leader of the Phalangist Party, who united the Maronite militias of Lebanon. His party emerged victorious from the 1982 Lebanon War with Israeli support and the expulsion of the PLO.
